recognize_zh: 紅色箭頭所指的多顆紅血球內各含一個小而圓、深紫色、偏心的點狀包涵體，即 Howell-Jolly 小體（核殘留），數量多時代表脾功能低下，此例與慢性移植物抗宿主病（cGVHD）造成的功能性無脾有關。
features: Multiple red cells containing a single small, round, dense purple inclusion (Howell-Jolly bodies), marked by arrows
One larger bluish (polychromatophilic) red cell also contains a Howell-Jolly body
Scattered echinocytes/crenated red cells and occasional target-like cells
Red cells otherwise largely normocytic with central pallor
Few platelets; no leukocytes in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows normocytic red cells with numerous Howell-Jolly bodies, appearing as single small, round, dense basophilic inclusions within red cells, including one in a polychromatophilic cell. Scattered crenated red cells are also present. No schistocytes, parasites, or nucleated red cells are seen in this field. Frequent Howell-Jolly bodies indicate hyposplenism, and in this clinical setting are consistent with functional asplenia related to chronic graft-versus-host disease, conferring increased risk of infection with encapsulated organisms.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are multiple, smaller, irregular granules clustered at the cell periphery and stain with Prussian blue, whereas Howell-Jolly bodies are single, round and larger.
Parasites show a cytoplasmic ring with a chromatin dot rather than a solid dense sphere.
An overlying platelet is larger, granular, and has a surrounding halo, and it lies in a different focal plane.
Stippling appears as numerous fine dots dispersed throughout the red cell rather than one discrete round body.
